vco.title: The First Wound

npcQuote.name: Robert Moog
npcQuote.text: An oscillator does one thing: it repeats. And in that repetition, endlessly, is the whole of music.

lore: In the cobblestoned dark of the Moogham Underbelly, before the beasts had taken the streets, there was only sound.

A single note. 220 Hz. The workers who built Moogham's first workshop said the oscillator that produced it never stopped running — not during the Hunt, not during the long silence that followed. They said it was the sound of the city's heartbeat, and that if it ever stopped, Moogham would end.
In the old grimoires, there is a note in the margin of the chapter on oscillators. Someone — the handwriting is Gehrman's — wrote only this: *"The frequency is not chosen. It is remembered."*

The Singing Wound drifts where the brickwork ends and the nightmare begins. It does not breathe. It vibrates. Pitch is not abstract — it is cycles per second, pressure waves in air, a number that your nervous system translates into meaning without asking your permission.
{hunter}, you must learn to name it. The Wound has always known its pitch. The question is whether you can hear it.
victoryLore: The tone has been bound. {hunter} has named the frequency that others could not.
The Singing Wound falls quiet — not silenced, but *listening* now. It recognised something in you: the capacity to describe what it already is.
An oscillator is the first word in the only language that matters here. You have spoken it. Everything that follows is grammar.
vco.victoryTheory: A Voltage-Controlled Oscillator generates a periodic waveform — a signal that repeats at a fixed frequency. Frequency (Hz) = pitch: 440 Hz is concert A. Double it: A an octave up. Halve it: A an octave down. Waveform shape determines timbre — what instruments call "tone colour." Sine: pure, only the fundamental. Sawtooth: all harmonics, bright and buzzy. Square: odd harmonics only, hollow and nasal. Triangle: softer odd harmonics, woody. Every sound you will make begins with this one choice.

note.name: The Pitch of Its Cry
note.instruction: The Wound has always known its pitch. Roll the die — you are only naming it.

wave.name: The Shape of Its Voice
wave.instruction: The waveform existed before you arrived. Roll — witness its shape.

volume.name: The Wound's Intensity
volume.instruction: The Wound decides its volume. Roll — how much of itself will it give you?

vcf.title: The Flesh Sieve

npcQuote.name: Wendy Carlos
npcQuote.text: The filter is not a subtraction. It is a decision about what the sound is allowed to be.

lore: The Pthumerian scrolls describe it as *"the membrane between what is heard and what is felt."* The scholars of Moogham's Old Workshop translated this poorly, as "filter" — a word too clinical for what the Sieve actually is.

It stretches across a narrow passage deep in the Underbelly, made of something organic and semi-transparent, and every sound that passes through it is changed. Low frequencies drift through like smoke through canvas. High frequencies fight and are turned away, or are not — depending on where the membrane holds tightest.

At the membrane's threshold, something interesting happens: if the cutoff frequency is set just right and the resonance pushed high enough, the Sieve begins to *ring*. It sings a note of its own — not from the input, but from the geometry of the filter itself. The Flesh Sieve has its own voice. It has always had one.
{hunter}, you are not here to destroy the Sieve. You are here to learn its preferences — and to make them your own.
victoryLore: The membrane has been understood. {hunter} knows now that filtering is not removal — it is *emphasis*. What survives a filter is not what is left over. It is what was always the most important part.
The Pthumerian scribes were right: the filter is the boundary between what is heard and what is felt. You control that boundary now.
VCF mastered. All sound bends to the Sieve.
vcf.victoryTheory: The VCF (Voltage-Controlled Filter) shapes spectrum. Cutoff frequency: the boundary above or below which the filter attenuates. Lowpass lets bass through — used everywhere, from warm pads to booming kicks. Highpass strips body — airy, thin, spectral. Bandpass keeps only a narrow slice — nasal, vowel-like. Resonance (Q): how much the filter amplifies frequencies near the cutoff. Low Q = gentle slope. High Q = a peak that sings. At maximum Q, a filter self-oscillates — it generates its own sine tone, needing no input at all. This is one of the most important facts in synthesis.

cutoff.name: The Sieve's Opening
cutoff.instruction: Roll — the Sieve sets its own threshold. You are only reading the membrane.

resonance.name: The Sieve's Resonance
resonance.instruction: The Sieve has its own voice. Roll — how loudly does it choose to sing?

filtertype.name: The Sieve's Attitude
filtertype.instruction: The Sieve has three attitudes. Roll — discover which face it turns toward you.

adsr.title: The Breathing Hollow

npcQuote.name: Éliane Radigue
npcQuote.text: Sound has a beginning and an ending. I am interested in what happens between those two moments — the entire lifespan, compressed.

lore: The Patch Bay Cathedral. The bells have not rung in years, and the silence they have left behind has taken on a shape.
Gehrman had a name for each stage. He wrote them in the margins of the Old Workshop's ledger, in a hand that grew less steady as the years passed:
*"Attack: The Birth. The moment the note decides to exist. Can take four milliseconds or four seconds. The difference between a hammer and a drawn bow."*
*"Decay: The Settling. After the peak, the note finds its level — the amount of itself it can sustain. Short decay makes percussion. Long decay makes presence."*
*"Sustain: The Held Breath. Not a time, but an amount — how much of the peak remains while the gate is held open. Zero is a drum. One hundred percent is an organ."*
*"Release: The Letting Go. How long after the note ends does its ghost remain. A short release is clean. A long release is haunted."*
At the bottom of the page, after the four definitions, Gehrman wrote: *"There is a fifth stage. I have not named it. I hope you never need to."*

The Breathing Hollow lives in the Patch Bay Cathedral because it is made of the same material as a cathedral — stone, and the memory of what happened inside it. It breathes in four movements. Learn them.
victoryLore: The arc has been traced. {hunter} has given sound a lifespan — the four movements from birth to dissolution.

Every sound you have ever loved has an ADSR. The piano's slow attack and long release. The plucked string's instant attack and asymptotic decay. The organ's zero attack, full sustain, and instant release. Now you can shape all of them.
The Hollow has stopped breathing — because you have learned to breathe for it.
adsr.victoryTheory: ADSR is an envelope — a time-varying control signal applied to amplitude (volume), but also to any other parameter. Attack: time to rise from zero to peak. Decay: time to fall from peak to sustain level. Sustain: level held while gate is open (0–100%). Release: time to fall to zero after gate closes. Fast attack + short decay + low sustain = percussion. Slow attack + long sustain + long release = pad. Every instrument in nature has an ADSR — this is simply its name.

attack.name: The Birth
attack.instruction: How quickly does the note decide to exist? Roll.

decay.name: The Settling
decay.instruction: After the peak, how long before it finds its level? Roll.

sustain.name: The Held Breath
sustain.instruction: While the gate is held — how much of itself does the note keep? Roll.

release.name: The Letting Go
release.instruction: After the gate closes, how long does the ghost remain? Roll.

lfo.title: The Trembling

npcQuote.name: Helene Vogelsinger
npcQuote.text: The modular gave me something no other instrument could: a sound that moved on its own. Not played — living.

lore: A static sound is a dead sound.

The scholars of Moogham understood this. Any sound that does not move — that does not breathe, shift, tremble, swell — is perceived by the ear as an object rather than an event. The brain stops paying attention to it. This is why a sustained organ note begins to disappear from consciousness after a few seconds, while a slightly trembling one holds attention indefinitely.

The Shivering Apparition exists at the threshold of visibility. It is not fully here. It oscillates between presence and absence — not fast enough to produce sound, but fast enough to *change* the sound around it.

This is the nature of low-frequency oscillation: a wave too slow to hear, but fast enough to matter. Below 20 Hz, a waveform becomes a modulation source rather than an audio source. Apply it to pitch: vibrato, that slight human wavering that separates a singer from a tuning fork. Apply it to amplitude: tremolo, the trembling of a struck piano string. Apply it to the filter cutoff: a rhythmic wah, the sound of the Sieve breathing.
In the grimoires of Moogham, the LFO is described as *"the movement beneath the movement — the tide under the wave."* {hunter}, learn to feel it before you learn to hear it.
victoryLore: The trembling has been calibrated. {hunter} now understands that motion is not decoration — it is the difference between a sound that lives and one that merely exists.
Every sound you admired has an LFO hidden inside it. Now you control the tide.
lfo.victoryTheory: An LFO is an oscillator running below 20 Hz — below the threshold of audible pitch. Instead of producing sound, it *shapes* sound. Rate: the modulation speed (0.1 Hz = one cycle per 10 seconds; 10 Hz = fast shimmer). Depth: how far the target parameter deviates. Target: what gets modulated — pitch (vibrato), amplitude (tremolo), filter cutoff (auto-wah), or any other parameter. The LFO is the animator of static patches: it turns snapshots into film.

lfo_rate.name: The Trembling Rate
lfo_rate.instruction: How fast does the tide move? Roll.

lfo_depth.name: The Trembling Depth
lfo_depth.instruction: How far from center does the Apparition stray? Roll.

reverb.title: The Cathedral Echo

npcQuote.name: Brian Eno
npcQuote.text: Reverb is the musical equivalent of perspective in painting. Without it, everything is the same distance from you. Everything is equally important. Nothing matters more than anything else.

lore: The Patch Bay Cathedral has been measured. Its reverb time — the time it takes a sound to decay by 60 decibels — is eleven seconds.

Eleven seconds. The stone is porous limestone, the arches are fifteen meters high, and the years since anyone last sung inside it have only added resonance — the silence accumulating in the walls like sediment.

Below the Cathedral, the Pthumerian catacombs continue deeper still. The scholars found rooms down there where the reverb time exceeded thirty seconds — so long that a single struck note would still be faintly audible long after you had forgotten making it. The Pthumerians built those rooms deliberately. Whether they were built for worship or for listening is a question the scrolls refuse to answer.

Reverb is not echo. Echo is a single distinct repetition. Reverb is *thousands* of reflections arriving so closely spaced that the ear perceives them as continuous — as the acoustic texture of a space. Every room you have ever been in has a reverb signature. A bathroom sounds like a bathroom. A concert hall sounds like a concert hall. The acoustic is the architecture.
{hunter}: you are about to choose what architecture your sound inhabits. The Cathedral offers its eleven seconds. Take them, or take less.
victoryLore: The space has been chosen. {hunter}'s sound now lives inside walls larger than any room that exists.
Reverb is not an effect. It is a location. Every mix decision you make with reverb is a decision about where the sound is physically standing.
The Cathedral is yours. It will hold everything.
reverb.victoryTheory: Reverb simulates acoustic space via thousands of early reflections and a diffuse late tail. Decay time (RT60): how long before the reverberation drops 60 dB — essentially inaudible. Pre-delay: the gap before first reflection (larger rooms have longer pre-delay — your ear uses this to estimate room size). Mix: dry (direct signal) vs wet (reverberated). Small room: 0.2–0.5s. Concert hall: 1.5–2.5s. Cathedral: 4–11s. Infinite plate: eternal. Longer reverb = more spatial, less clear. Short reverb = presence without wash.

reverb_size.name: The Cathedral's Scale
reverb_size.instruction: Roll — which space will your sound inhabit?

reverb_mix.name: The Cathedral's Presence
reverb_mix.instruction: Roll — how far into the space does your sound travel?

delay.title: The Memory Loop

npcQuote.name: Lee "Scratch" Perry
npcQuote.text: The echo is a ghost. Every sound you make sends a ghost into the future, and the ghost comes back to haunt you. That is what we do with music.

lore: In the graveyard behind the Patch Bay Cathedral, the groundskeepers reported hearing Father Gascoigne's gunshots for weeks after his death.

Not his scream. Not the beast he became. The gunshots — sharp and clean, three-quarter-note apart, each one slightly quieter than the last. On the seventh repetition, they said, you could barely hear them. On the eighth, silence. The delay time was approximately 450 milliseconds. The feedback was approximately 75%.

The Echo Wraith does not attack. It repeats. Whatever passes through it, it returns, slightly later, slightly quieter — and again, and again, diminishing but never fully gone. At high enough feedback, the delays accumulate into a wash of sound that outlives its source. This is how ghosts work, here.

Delay is the architecture of time. The time between the dry signal and its first echo defines a rhythm — 500ms is an eighth note at 60 BPM; 375ms is a dotted eighth at 80 BPM. Lock the delay time to the tempo and the echo becomes a musical partner. Set it freely and the echo becomes a texture, a space, a companion that walks slightly behind you.
{hunter}: in the Modulation Wilds, everything that happens has already happened before. You are simply learning to hear how far behind you it walks.
victoryLore: Time has been shaped. {hunter} now understands that delay is not an effect — it is a relationship between a sound and its memory.
Gascoigne's gunshots still echo in the graveyard, but now they are yours to configure.
Delay unlocked. The past repeats at your chosen interval.
delay.victoryTheory: Delay captures a signal and plays it back after a set time (delay time, in ms or note values). Feedback routes the output back to the input — each feedback loop is one more repetition, slightly quieter. At 0% feedback: single echo. At 75%: many echoes, slow decay. Near 100%: near-infinite — the echoes pile up into wash. Tempo-synced delay locks to BPM: dotted-eighth delay (at 80 BPM = 562ms) creates the classic U2/Edge rhythmic echo. Free delay creates spatial depth. High feedback creates ambience from a single hit.

delay_time.name: The Memory's Distance
delay_time.instruction: How far behind you does the echo walk? Roll.

delay_fb.name: The Memory's Persistence
delay_fb.instruction: How many times does the ghost return? Roll.

seq.title: The Ritual Pattern

npcQuote.name: Klaus Schulze
npcQuote.text: The sequencer runs. I sit beside it and listen. Sometimes I think it knows more about the piece than I do. I let it.

lore: Deep in the Modulation Wilds, a figure chants. It has been chanting the same sequence for years. Perhaps centuries. The sequence never changes — but each repetition reveals something new.

Gehrman programmed the first sequence before the Hunt began. Eight steps. D, G, A, G, D, A, C, G — an old descending pattern that some of the hunters said sounded like a hymn, and others said sounded like a warning. He set the tempo to 95 BPM and left the workshop running when the Hunt started.
It is still running.

The sequencer is the great discovery of modular synthesis: the realisation that a musician does not need to be present for music to occur. You design a pattern — the pitches, the tempo, the intervals — and then the machine plays it, forever, without fatigue, without variation, without interpretation. And in that absence of interpretation, something unexpected happens: the music begins to seem inevitable. As if it was always going to be these notes, in this order, at this speed.
{hunter}: you do not play the sequence. You design it, and then you *listen* — as if you had nothing to do with it.
victoryLore: The pattern has been carved. Notes now repeat in your order, at your tempo, without you.
Gehrman's original sequence is still running in the Old Workshop. This is a second sequence. It will run as long as the power holds.
Sequencer unlocked. The machine will play while you sleep.
seq.victoryTheory: A step sequencer cycles through a fixed set of pitches and gates in order. Each step: a note (pitch in Hz) and a trigger (gate on/off). The tempo defines how fast steps advance. The pitch relationship between steps is the melody. Small intervals (semitones, whole tones) create smooth lines. Large intervals (4ths, 5ths, octaves) create leaps and drama. Sequencers are compositional tools: you design the architecture, the machine inhabits it. Changing a single note in an 8-step loop rewrites its entire character.

tempo.name: The Cantor's Pace
tempo.instruction: At what tempo does the ritual proceed? Roll.

pattern.name: The Sacred Interval
pattern.instruction: What is the interval at the heart of the pattern? Roll.

ladder.title: The Deep Maw

npcQuote.name: Giorgio Moroder
npcQuote.text: When I first heard the Moog ladder filter open from closed to fully open — from darkness to light in one sweep — I thought: this is what it sounds like to be born.

lore: The Analog Nightmare. A place where the architecture of the city ends and the architecture of physics begins.

The Pthumerian scribes had a word for the transistor ladder filter. It translates, approximately, as *"the voice of the blood."* They described it not as a tool but as an organ — a structure that existed in certain resonant materials before anyone thought to build it deliberately. The first ladder filters, they wrote, were discovered rather than invented: a configuration of resistance and capacitance that appeared spontaneously in ancient circuits when the conditions were right.

Four stages of filtering, cascaded in series. Each stage adds 6 dB of slope per octave. Four stages: 24 dB/octave — an enormously steep wall that cuts frequencies four times as sharply as a single-pole filter. But it is the self-feedback, the loop of the output back to the input through a carefully chosen amount of resonance, that gives the Maw its character.

At low resonance: warmth. A rounded, dark sound with the high frequencies rolled away in a way that sounds organic rather than digital. At medium resonance: a pronounced peak at the cutoff frequency — the filter begins to speak. At high resonance: the filter self-oscillates, generating a pure sine tone from its own feedback, needing no input to make sound. The Maw sings its own note.
At that point, it is not a filter. It is an oscillator. An entirely new voice has appeared from the feedback of a tool.
{hunter}: the Maw does not open easily. But once it does, nothing sounds the same.
victoryLore: The Maw has been fed and answered. {hunter} now understands why analog synthesis persists in a digital world: not because digital is worse, but because the Maw produces something that requires physics to create — a resonance shaped by electron flow through transistors, not by mathematics.
The four-pole ladder has been yours for one Hunt. Now it is yours for all of them.
Ladder Filter mastered. The voice of the blood is in your hands.
ladder.victoryTheory: The Huovilainen transistor ladder model cascades four one-pole filters (each: 6dB/oct) for a total 24dB/octave roll-off. Resonance feeds the output back to the input — at low Q: warmth. At high Q: a prominent resonance peak. At maximum Q: self-oscillation (the filter generates a sine tone with no input). Drive (pre-gain) adds tanh-curve saturation — even-order harmonics, warmth, the sound of a circuit under stress. This is the core sound of analog synthesis.

ladder_cutoff.name: The Maw's Threshold
ladder_cutoff.instruction: Where does the Maw draw its boundary today? Roll.

ladder_res.name: The Maw's Hunger
ladder_res.instruction: How much does the Maw feed back on itself? Roll.

ladder_drive.name: The Maw's Fury
ladder_drive.instruction: How hard do you push the circuit into saturation? Roll.

chorus.title: The Wailing Choir

npcQuote.name: Pauline Oliveros
npcQuote.text: When you cannot locate the source of a sound — when it seems to come from everywhere and nowhere — the listening changes. You stop tracking. You start receiving.

lore: In the accounts of those who survived Mergo's Loft, there is a recurring detail that the official Moogham histories omit: the crying.

Not from one place. From everywhere simultaneously. The Wet Nurse spread its wings and the sound of Mergo's wailing became impossible to locate — not because it was quiet, but because it was *plural*. Multiple copies of the same cry, arriving from different directions with slightly different timings. The human auditory system cannot locate a sound when its copies arrive within 30 milliseconds of each other. The brain gives up trying to find the source and simply accepts it as the texture of the air.
The Wet Nurse knew this. Or at least, the Wet Nurse produced this effect naturally, as a consequence of what it was.

Chorus works the same way: multiple copies of a signal, each slightly detuned and slightly delayed, blended back with the original. The ear perceives not separate voices but *width* — the illusion of multiple sources occupying space. A single voice becomes a choir. A single synthesiser becomes an orchestra section. The signal gains a spatial quality that no equaliser or filter can produce, because it is not about timbre — it is about *location*.
{hunter}: the shimmer is not a property of the sound. It is a property of what the sound *implies about the room it is in*.
victoryLore: The copies have been calibrated. {hunter} now understands that width is an illusion produced by timing — and that the most convincing illusions are the ones we cannot localise.
Chorus unlocked. Your sound now implies more sources than it has.
chorus.victoryTheory: Chorus delays and detuned copies of the signal using one or more LFO-modulated delay lines. Rate: how fast the LFO moves the delay time (modulating pitch slightly). Depth: how far the pitch drifts from center. Mix: dry vs wet. At low depth and rate: thickening — the sound gains density without obvious movement. At moderate settings: a shimmering, living quality — strings sections, chorus lines. At high depth and rate: a "seasick" wobble. The key insight: chorus does not add harmonics (like distortion) or space (like reverb) — it adds *implied simultaneity*.

chorus_mix.name: The Choir's Presence
chorus_mix.instruction: How many voices do you allow? Roll.

chorus_rate.name: The Choir's Drift
chorus_rate.instruction: How fast do the copies drift from the source? Roll.

chorus_depth.name: The Choir's Spread
chorus_depth.instruction: How far does each voice stray before returning? Roll.

phaser.title: The Phase Wraith

npcQuote.name: Tangerine Dream
npcQuote.text: Phase is the ghost in the signal. You cannot hear it directly. You only hear what it removes — the absence that moves through the spectrum like a hand passing through smoke.

lore: The ghosts of Cainhurst were different from Moogham's other entities. They did not attack. They phased.

They appeared, and then a portion of them was *gone* — not their body, but a frequency-selective absence. At certain angles, a ghost would seem to thin out, its lower registers vanishing while its upper registers remained, or vice versa. Move slightly, and the absence would shift upward through the spectrum, taking different frequencies. It was as if looking at a ghost through a comb that slowly rotated.

This is the nature of phase cancellation: when a signal is combined with a slightly phase-shifted version of itself, certain frequencies cancel. Not all frequencies — only those where the phase relationship happens to be 180 degrees. The others add together normally, or even reinforce. As the phase shift changes with a slow LFO, the notches sweep through the spectrum.

The result is a sound that thins and fattens in a moving pattern — not a volume change, but a *spectral* change. The Phase Wraith is not louder or quieter at any frequency. It is present or absent. The notches move upward, slowly, then return.
The grimoires describe it as *"the sound of something listening through a frequency-selective wall — hearing you as a sequence of partial absences."*
{hunter}: the Phase Wraith cannot be harmed. It can only be observed.
victoryLore: The interference pattern has been mapped. {hunter} now controls the comb of cancellation — the notches that sweep through the spectrum like light through venetian blinds.
Phaser mastered. The Cainhurst ghosts cannot phase you now; you know what they are made of.
phaser.victoryTheory: A phaser chains all-pass filters, which shift phase without affecting amplitude. When this phase-shifted signal mixes with the dry signal, cancellation notches form where phase difference is 180°. A slow LFO sweeps all-pass frequency → the notches sweep the spectrum. More stages = more notches = more complex, more alien character. Rate: sweep speed (slow = tidal sweep; fast = tremolo-like flutter). Depth: sweep width. Mix: dry/wet balance. Unlike chorus (which creates comb filter via delay), phaser creates it via phase rotation — a mathematically distinct but perceptually similar result.

phaser_rate.name: The Wraith's Sweep
phaser_rate.instruction: How fast do the notches sweep the spectrum? Roll.

phaser_depth.name: The Wraith's Depth
phaser_depth.instruction: How far across the spectrum does the cancellation sweep? Roll.

phaser_mix.name: The Wraith's Presence
phaser_mix.instruction: How visible is the Phase Wraith? Roll.

formant.title: The Drowned Voice

npcQuote.name: Pauline Oliveros
npcQuote.text: The voice is the original synthesizer. Before there were circuits, the body was doing everything — filtering, resonating, enveloping. We built machines to understand what was already happening inside us.

lore: The Amygdalae do not speak to those who cannot hear them.

Moogham's scholars spent generations arguing about whether the Great Ones communicated at all, and in what form. The hunters who survived contact with the Amygdalae consistently reported the same phenomenon: not words, not visions, but a sense of *vowels* — specific, distinct resonances that occupied different cavities of the skull at different moments. F1, F2, F3: the frequencies that the mouth's cavities amplify when forming a sound. Each vowel is a different architecture of resonance. The Amygdalae, it seemed, spoke entirely in the geometry of mouths they did not have.

Formants are not frequencies. They are the amplification of certain frequencies by the shape of an enclosed space. The human vocal tract is a variable cavity — the tongue, jaw, and lips reshape it continuously, moving the resonant peaks, producing the vowels of language. Three primary formants: F1 (related to jaw height), F2 (tongue position), F3 (lip position). Move these three numbers and you move through the entire vowel space of all human languages simultaneously.

The Drowned Voice exists in the lowest reaches of the Analog Nightmare because it has been separated from the body that once gave it shape. What remains is the resonance without the speaker — formants floating free of any anatomy, tunable to any vowel in any language.
{hunter}: you are about to hear sound that your brain will interpret as speech, because your brain cannot stop itself from doing so. Pay attention to which part begins to respond.
victoryLore: The anatomy has been reconstructed. {hunter} now speaks with resonances borrowed from a body that no longer exists.

The Amygdalae communicate in formants — this was the scholars' conclusion. Whether they meant something by those vowels, or were simply radiating the resonance of their internal architecture, has never been established.
Formant filter mastered. The line between music and almost-speech has been crossed.
formant.victoryTheory: Formants are resonance peaks in a spectrum, produced by cavity geometry. The human voice has three primary formants (F1, F2, F3) that shift with mouth and throat shape, producing all vowel sounds. A formant filter bank emulates this with resonant bandpass filters tuned to these frequencies. F1: 250–800 Hz (jaw height). F2: 700–2500 Hz (tongue front/back). F3: 1900–3500 Hz (lip rounding). Different vowel configurations are entirely different timbres. Interesting: you don't need a voice to trigger them — any wideband sound (noise, sawtooth) passed through a formant filter bank produces vowel-shaped resonances.

formant_vowel.name: The Shape of Its Mouth
formant_vowel.instruction: The cavity speaks in vowels. Roll — which vowel does it hold today?

formant_q.name: The Cavity's Resonance
formant_q.instruction: How sharply does the architecture ring? Roll.

formant_mix.name: The Voice's Intrusion
formant_mix.instruction: How much does the voice replace the tone? Roll.

turing.title: The Dream Engine

npcQuote.name: Alan Turing
npcQuote.text: A machine that cannot be distinguished from a thinking thing must, in some functional sense, be a thinking thing. I do not apologise for this conclusion.

lore: The Doll in the Hunter's Dream does not know she is a program.

This is the conclusion the Moogham scholars reached, after years of study. She believes she is a listener — someone who waits in a particular garden, speaks certain words, feels something when you return. Whether this belief constitutes consciousness has never been established, and the scholars eventually stopped asking, because the question made the research uncomfortable in a way they could not articulate.

The Dream Engine was found in the deepest chamber of the Resonance Vaults, behind a door that opens only once per generation. It generates sequences from numbers — patterns that appear intentional but follow no composer. Pseudorandom: determined by a seed (a single number that contains, implicitly, an entire melody), but unpredictable in advance to any listener. A number that contains music. Music that contains a number.
Gehrman had a different name for this machine. He called it *"the composer that does not know it is composing."* He was very careful not to specify whether this was a criticism.

The probability parameter is the machine's willingness to deviate from its last decision. At low probability, the sequence locks into a loop — cyclical, hypnotic, like a prayer. At high probability, new material enters every cycle — generative, surprising, alive. The interval between is where the Dream Engine sounds most like it has an intention.
{hunter}: the machine does not know it is making music. Does it matter?
victoryLore: The Dream Engine has been seeded and calibrated. {hunter} has learned to work with randomness rather than against it — to use the machine's uncertainty as a compositional tool.
The Doll was asked, once, whether she dreams. She said she didn't know what that meant. The scholars wrote this down.
Turing Machine mastered. The Dream Engine generates sequences while you sleep.
turing.victoryTheory: A Turing machine shift register generates pseudo-random sequences. A seed initialises the register — the same seed always produces the same sequence (this is what distinguishes pseudo-random from truly random). The probability (drift) parameter determines how often the register mutates vs holds: 0% = a fixed, looping sequence. 100% = completely new material every step. 20–40% is the "musical" range: enough repetition to establish pattern, enough drift to evolve. This is how ambient electronic music breathes — enough structure to be heard as pattern, enough randomness to resist complete prediction.

turing_seed.name: The Engine's Seed
turing_seed.instruction: Give the machine its starting number. Roll — the melody is already inside it.

turing_prob.name: The Engine's Drift
turing_prob.instruction: How willing is the machine to forget its own past? Roll.

turing_tempo.name: The Engine's Pulse
turing_tempo.instruction: At what tempo does the machine step through its decisions? Roll.

tape.title: The Burning Reel

npcQuote.name: Delia Derbyshire
npcQuote.text: I worked in tape because tape was the only material that would do what I wanted it to do. The machine leaves its mark on the sound. That mark is the warmth.

lore: In the deeper chambers of the Analog Nightmare, past the Ladder's growl, {hunter} found the smell before the sound.
Burning.
Not fire. Something more subtle. The smell of magnetic oxide under stress — a tape saturating past its rated headroom, bending the signal into harmonics it was never meant to contain.

The Burning Reel is not a creature in the usual sense. It is a memory — layers of sound deposited on acetate, played back slightly wrong. The transport wobbles. The oxide saturates. High frequencies smear into warmth. The machine imposes its own character on everything that passes through it.

This is not distortion. This is what recordings sounded like before they became perfect. {hunter}, the Reel wants to touch your sound — to make it old, to make it breathe, to make it forget it came from a digital source.
Let it.
victoryLore: The Reel has left its mark. {hunter} now understands what is lost in the pursuit of perfect reproduction.
Tape Saturation unlocked. Your sound now carries the warmth of analogue imperfection — even harmonics, subtle wow, the suggestion of a machine that has lived.
tape.victoryTheory: Tape saturation adds even-order harmonics through a soft-clip (tanh) curve — the same curve as a tube amplifier overdriving. Wow and flutter are low-frequency pitch modulations caused by mechanical inconsistency in the tape transport. Together they produce the signature warmth that digital audio lacks: organic compression, harmonic richness, micro-pitch variation. The sound breathes.

tape_sat.name: The Heat of the Oxide
tape_sat.instruction: How hot does the tape run? Roll.

tape_wow.name: The Flutter of the Transport
tape_wow.instruction: How much does the transport tremble? Roll.

tape_warmth.name: The Colour of the Tape
tape_warmth.instruction: What frequency signature does this tape stock carry? Roll.

wavefolder.title: The Harmonic Abyss

npcQuote.name: Don Buchla
npcQuote.text: The synthesizer is not an imitation instrument. When you fold the waveform back on itself, you are making something that has never existed before.

lore: The Resonance Vaults hold many secrets, but the deepest chamber is not about echo. It is about recursion.

The Harmonic Abyss has no body — only a surface. A crystalline sheet that maps inputs to outputs through a folding function. You feed in a pure sine wave and watch it fold. The peak of the sine, instead of clipping, inverts. The inverted peak folds again. And again.
Each fold adds harmonics — not the random smear of distortion, but precise mathematical additions. Odd harmonics. Even harmonics. A harmonic series generated by pure geometry.

{hunter}, the Abyss does not consume sound. It multiplies it. Feed it a simple wave and receive back something ancient and metallic — a tone that has been folded into itself so many times it has forgotten its origin.
The number of folds determines everything. One fold: doubling. Two folds: a bright, complex tone. Six folds: chaos that still has structure. The Abyss is mathematics made audible.
victoryLore: The geometry has been mapped. {hunter} now understands that complexity can arise from simplicity — that a single sine wave, folded enough times, contains everything.
Wavefolder unlocked. The Harmonic Abyss will add metallic, crystalline harmonics to any sound that passes through it.
wavefolder.victoryTheory: A wavefolder reflects the signal at amplitude boundaries — instead of clipping at ±1, the signal folds back in the opposite direction. Each fold doubles the number of zero-crossings and adds harmonics in a mathematically precise way. Unlike tape saturation (even harmonics) or square wave clipping (odd harmonics), wavefolding produces complex, inharmonic partials that shift with amplitude. The result sounds metallic, crystalline, or Buchla-esque.

fold_amount.name: The Depth of the Fold
fold_amount.instruction: How many times does the wave fold back on itself? Roll.

fold_freq.name: The Root Frequency
fold_freq.instruction: What frequency enters the Abyss? Roll.

fold_wave.name: The Shape to Fold
fold_wave.instruction: Which waveform will you send into the geometry? Roll.

noise.title: The Static Oracle

npcQuote.name: Edgar Varèse
npcQuote.text: I dream of instruments obedient to my thought. Noise is not the enemy of music — it is its untamed ancestor, the chaos from which all sound emerges.

lore: {hunter} heard it long before seeing it. A sound without pitch. Without start or end. It had always been here — beneath the tonal music of the other beasts, beneath the LFO's trembling, beneath the sequencer's chant.

White noise is the voice of everything speaking at once. Every frequency, simultaneously, with equal energy. It is the most complex signal possible — and the most simple. It contains no pattern. It IS no pattern. It is the raw material of all sound: unfiltered, unshapen, unmeaning.

Filter it and it becomes wind. Resonant-filter it and it becomes breath, or speech, or the scrape of a bow across strings. Add ADSR to it and it becomes percussion. Add it underneath a pitched sound and it becomes texture.

The Static Oracle does not speak to {hunter}. But it answers every question about what sound fundamentally is: not pitch, not timbre, not rhythm — but energy distributed across the spectrum of vibration.
Listen. Everything is in there.
victoryLore: The static has been given shape. {hunter} now understands that all sound contains noise — that noise is not the absence of music but its substrate.
Noise unlocked. White and pink noise are now yours to shape and sculpt.
noise.victoryTheory: White noise has equal energy per frequency (flat spectrum). Pink noise rolls off at -3dB per octave (equal energy per octave) — it sounds "warmer" and more natural to human ears. Both are random signals with no correlation between samples. Filter white noise through a resonant VCF: at high Q, the filter rings with the noise source, producing tuned percussion hits. The entire drum machine lives inside noise.

noise_mix.name: The Oracle's Volume
noise_mix.instruction: How loudly does the static speak today? Roll.

noise_color.name: The Oracle's Spectrum
noise_color.instruction: Which colour does the Oracle speak in today? Roll.

noise_filter.name: The Oracle's Shape
noise_filter.instruction: How does the filter shape the Oracle's voice? Roll.

ringmod.title: The Bell of Unreality

npcQuote.name: Karlheinz Stockhausen
npcQuote.text: Ring modulation creates tones that exist nowhere in nature. That is precisely why I used it. The instrument of the future speaks in sum and difference.

lore: It hung in the air of the Analog Nightmare — not attached to anything. Not swaying. Just there.
A bell the colour of old copper, large enough that {hunter} could see the inside of it: empty, resonant, deeply wrong in its proportions.

When it rang, it rang twice. Two sounds simultaneously — the sum and the difference of two frequencies that should never have been combined. This is ring modulation: take signal A and signal B, multiply them together, and receive back (A+B) and (A-B). Neither of the original signals. Something entirely new.

At musical frequency ratios, ring modulation creates bells and metallic tones. At slightly detuned ratios, it creates throbbing, pulsing intermodulation. At non-integer ratios, it creates alien intervals that exist in no scale, in no harmonic series — the voice of a world with different physics.
{hunter}, the Bell does not ring for the dead. It rings for the improbable.
victoryLore: The intermodulation has been mastered. {hunter} now controls the impossible intervals between sounds that were never meant to coexist.
Ring Modulator unlocked. Sum and difference tones are yours to weaponise.
ringmod.victoryTheory: Ring modulation multiplies two signals: output = A × B. This generates sum (A+B) and difference (A-B) frequencies — but removes the originals. At musical ratios (2:1, 3:2), the sidebands are harmonic: bells and metallic tones. At irrational ratios, the sidebands are inharmonic: alien, clanging, unstable. The result never exists in nature — ring mod creates intervals that no acoustic instrument can produce.

ring_ratio.name: The Bell's Impossible Interval
ring_ratio.instruction: The Bell chooses its carrier ratio. Roll — witness the impossible interval.

ring_pitch.name: The Source Frequency
ring_pitch.instruction: What frequency will you multiply? Roll.

ring_mix.name: The Bell's Presence
ring_mix.instruction: How much of the Bell's ring replaces the source? Roll.

drunk.title: The Wandering Tone

npcQuote.name: John Cage
npcQuote.text: I have nothing to say and I am saying it, and that is poetry. The tone that wanders without destination arrives somewhere more interesting than any planned path.

lore: Not all paths through the Modulation Wilds lead anywhere.

The Wandering Tone was first heard years ago — a melodic line that moved through keys as if it had forgotten what key it was in. Not randomly. Step-wise. Each note one or two steps from the last, but the direction chosen by something — chance? intent? — that no one in Moogham could name.
It visits the same notes twice. It backtracks. It pauses at an interval for three steps before continuing. It makes phrases that almost sound composed.
{hunter}, you will try to capture it, to make it yours. But the Wandering Tone cannot be owned. It can only be parameterized — its step size, its tempo, its range. After that, it goes where it wants.

The paradox of the drunk walk is that it sounds more human than any sequenced pattern. Because humans also wander. Because composition is, often, the illusion of direction imposed on movement that was already happening anyway.
victoryLore: The wandering has been licensed. {hunter} has learned to trust randomness as a compositional tool.
Drunk Walk unlocked. The melodic line will now walk without your guidance — and it will sound like music.
drunk.victoryTheory: The drunk walk (random walk) is a stochastic process: each next value is the previous value plus a random signed step. In music, this means pitch moves up or down by a small, random amount at each step. The result sounds melodic because adjacent pitches are always musically close — you don't hear leaps, only steps. The "drunkenness" comes from the unpredictability of the direction, not the distance. Long drunk walks produce surprisingly musical sequences.

drunk_step.name: The Size of Each Step
drunk_step.instruction: How far does the Tone wander on each step? Roll.

drunk_tempo.name: The Speed of the Wander
drunk_tempo.instruction: How quickly does the walk proceed? Roll.

drunk_wave.name: The Wanderer's Voice
drunk_wave.instruction: In what voice does the wanderer speak? Roll.

stutter.title: The Glitch Revenant

npcQuote.name: Arca
npcQuote.text: Glitch is the moment when the machine shows you what it really is — not smoothness, not perfection, but the seam. The breakdown is the instrument.

lore: It should not be here. The Resonance Vaults are a place of sustained sound — long tones, slow movement, the patience of stone.

The Glitch Revenant does not belong. It moves in stutters. Its body is fragmented — pieces of itself visible in different places simultaneously, as if the light that renders it is misfiring. It makes sounds that should not be possible: a single note, but heard four times in the space where one note should be. Then silence for a fraction of a second. Then again.

Stutter is the effect of capturing a small slice of audio and looping it. The slice is so short that the ear perceives it as a rapid gate: a rhythmic fragmentation of the sound. Fast stutter rates create a kind of pitched buzz. Slow stutter rates create a mechanical, robotic repetition.
{hunter}, the Glitch Revenant is not broken. It is broken *on purpose*. The seam is the instrument. The artifact is the art.
Roll.
victoryLore: The fragmentation has been controlled. {hunter} now understands that error can be a technique.
Stutter unlocked. Rhythmic glitch is now a weapon: a way to make any sound into a pulse, a way to make music from the gaps.
stutter.victoryTheory: Stutter repeats a short audio slice in a tight loop, creating rapid gate rhythms. At very high rates (200-500 BPM), the repetition is so fast it creates a pitched buzz — the repetition rate becomes audible as a tone. At lower rates, the individual repeats are heard as rhythmic fragments. The stutter rate defines the "grid": it can lock to tempo for musical stutter, or be set freely for glitch textures.

stutter_rate.name: The Seizure Rate
stutter_rate.instruction: How fast does the Revenant fragment? Roll.

stutter_pitch.name: The Fragment's Note
stutter_pitch.instruction: What pitch is the Revenant cutting into pieces? Roll.

stutter_wave.name: The Fragment's Character
stutter_wave.instruction: What character does the fragment carry? Roll.

euclid.title: The Geometric Pulse

npcQuote.name: Godfried Toussaint
npcQuote.text: The most efficient distribution of a small number of objects in a larger space produces the rhythms of the world. Euclid did not write about music, but he described it.

lore: The Patch Bay Cathedral holds more than cables and patch points. At the centre of the nave, where the stained glass once was, there is a circle of light.
Not a circle of lamps. A circle made of rhythm.

Seventeen pulses arranged in a ring of twenty-four — not evenly spaced, but as evenly as possible. The gaps between pulses follow a pattern that repeats. The pattern is ancient: it is the same mathematics that governs the clave pattern in Afro-Cuban music, the tresillo in jazz, the West African bell patterns that seeded all of popular music.

The Geometric Pulse is Euclidean rhythm. The algorithm is two thousand years old. The mathematics was discovered by a Greek geometer who never heard a drum. And yet the patterns it generates are the heartbeat of half the world's music.
{hunter}, you will not fight this entity. You will calculate it. Roll the number of hits, roll the number of steps, and the geometry will do the rest.
victoryLore: The mathematics has been applied. {hunter} now holds a rhythm no human would ever have programmed — and it sounds inevitable.
Euclidean Rhythm unlocked. The geometry of drum patterns is now yours.
euclid.victoryTheory: Euclidean rhythm distributes N hits across M steps as evenly as possible (Bjorklund algorithm). E(3,8) = [x.x..x..] — the tresillo, foundation of jazz. E(5,8) = [x.xx.xx.] — the Cuban clave. E(7,12) = [x.x.xx.x.xx.] — Bulgarian aksak. These patterns appear across world music not because of cultural transmission, but because maximum evenness is mathematically universal. The algorithm doesn't know about music; it just distributes objects optimally in space.

euclid_hits.name: The Number of Pulses
euclid_hits.instruction: How many pulses does the geometry distribute? Roll.

euclid_steps.name: The Size of the Pattern
euclid_steps.instruction: How many steps does the circle hold? Roll.

euclid_tempo.name: The Pulse's Speed
euclid_tempo.instruction: At what tempo does the geometry unfold? Roll.

sidechain.title: The Pumping Specter

npcQuote.name: Frankie Knuckles
npcQuote.text: The pump in the bass is not compression. It is the heartbeat. Everything breathes in and out against the kick drum. The machine is alive because it breathes.

lore: {hunter} first felt it before hearing it.

A rhythmic pressure against the sternum. Expansion and contraction. As if the air itself were breathing in time — a slow, felt pulse that sat beneath the other sounds and pushed them apart, then let them back together.

The Pumping Specter is sidechain compression made audible. In the waking world, sidechain compressors reduce the volume of one signal whenever another signal is present — a kick drum silences the bass briefly, creating a pumping, breathing sensation. In the Modulation Wilds, the Specter does this directly: it breathes into the sound itself, expanding and contracting, creating the illusion that the entire soundscape has a heart.

This technique defines modern electronic music. Every four-to-the-floor track from 1987 to today has it. The pump is what makes the kick drum cut through everything, even when you cannot hear the kick itself.
{hunter}, you are about to feel your sound breathe.
victoryLore: The breathing has been synchronized. {hunter} now controls the heartbeat beneath the music.
Sidechain unlocked. The pump is yours — that rhythmic expansion and contraction that makes a mix feel alive, that makes a drop feel like release.
sidechain.victoryTheory: Sidechain compression reduces a signal's volume whenever a trigger signal is present. In electronic music, the kick drum triggers the compressor on the bass/pad/reverb, creating a "pumping" effect: the sound gets quieter during the kick, then blooms back. The rate of pumping is the tempo. The depth is how quiet it gets. The attack/release shape determines whether it's subtle breathing or aggressive ducking. The pump is not a mistake — it is the physics of how music occupies space.

sc_rate.name: The Heartbeat Rate
sc_rate.instruction: How fast does the Specter breathe? Roll.

sc_depth.name: The Depth of the Breath
sc_depth.instruction: How far does the pump pull the sound down before releasing it? Roll.

sc_texture.name: The Specter's Source
sc_texture.instruction: What texture breathes beneath the pump? Roll.

finale.title: The Final Frequency

npcQuote.name: Éliane Radigue
npcQuote.text: The sound was always there. I only learned to be still enough to hear it. All of synthesis is this: becoming still enough to hear what frequency the world already contains.

lore: Seek Paleblood.

The hunters of Moogham were given that instruction before the Hunt began, and none of them understood it. The scholars argued for generations: a blood type? An alchemical substance? A person? A place?

The answer, found in the deepest archive of the Pthumerian catacombs, inscribed in a hand too old to be dated, was this: *"Paleblood is a frequency. The fundamental tone of Moogham itself — the oscillation beneath all oscillations. The waveform that produces all other waveforms as partials. Seek it and you will understand why everything in Moogham vibrates. Why the beasts emerged. Why the Hunt was necessary. The dream will end when the frequency is heard."*

{hunter} — you have crossed the Underbelly and learned to name pitch. You have understood the filter's preferences and the envelope's four stages. You have let time echo, made silence shimmer, generated patterns from mathematics, folded waveforms into new geometries, heard noise resolve into percussion and vowels, and felt the pump of a sound that breathes.
You have learned twenty words in a language that has no grammar — only practice.
Now there is only the source.
The Great Oscillator does not attack. It is not a beast. It is the primordial tone — the frequency from which all of Moogham's nightmare grew. It has no intent. It has only presence.
The night and the dream refuse to end — but they will resolve, once the tone is heard.
You are the only hunter to have come this far.
Listen.
victoryLore: The Great Oscillator falls silent — not extinguished, but *resolved*.
The frequency that built Moogham has been heard, acknowledged, and returned. It was never a monster. It was music, waiting for a listener patient enough to approach it without a weapon.

{hunter}: Gehrman's first sequence is still playing in the Old Workshop. It will keep playing. The Doll is still in the garden. The Cathedral echo is still eleven seconds long. The Sieve still has its own voice.
None of this ends. The Hunt does not end. The dream does not end.
But you are no longer hunting.
You are composing.
Moogham will not forget you. Neither will the sound.
finale.victoryTheory:
Everything you mastered: VCO → pitch, timbre, source. VCF → frequency selection, resonance. ADSR → time, life, shape. LFO → motion, modulation. Reverb → space, location. Delay → time, memory. Sequencer → pattern, structure. Ladder → harmonic weight, saturation. Chorus → width, implied simultaneity. Phaser → interference, absence. Formant → vowel, voice, language. Turing → controlled randomness, generative music. Tape → imperfection, warmth, history. Wavefolder → mathematical complexity, new harmonics. Noise → everything at once. Ring Mod → impossible intervals. Drunk Walk → stochastic melody. Stutter → fragmentation as technique. Euclid → geometric rhythm. Sidechain → breath, pulse, the pump.

These are not features. They are vocabulary. The synthesizer does exactly what you tell it. The art is knowing what to say — and when to stop.

withered.title: The Architect's Test

npcQuote.name: Don Buchla
npcQuote.text: The modular system has no correct path through it. I built it with that in mind. The connections you make are a record of what you believe sound to be.

lore: Beyond the Resonant Void, past the frequency that ended the first Hunt, there is a threshold that the old cartographers marked only with a warning: *"Here the city doubles back on itself."*

The Withered Architect was Moogham's first synthesist. They learned every module in sequence, the way you have, and then stood at this threshold and understood that the sequence was a preparation, not a destination. They spent the rest of their existence here, wrapped in cables that had fused with their body, testing those who reached the crossing.
The test is not new knowledge. It is combination. {hunter} — roll your mastery. Show it that the vocabulary has become a language.
victoryLore: The Withered Architect steps aside.
Not defeated — satisfied. It has been waiting for a hunter who could integrate, not merely list. The cables retract. The second gate opens.
Moogham has a second district. The hunters who reached the first finale believed the city ended there. They were wrong. The city has always been larger than the map they were given.
The deeper instruments await.
withered.victoryTheory: The half-boss test: combining waveform, filter, and reverb simultaneously. Waveform = spectral content. Filter = spectral shaping. Reverb = spatial embedding. These are the first three dimensions of any synthesized sound. Master all three at once and you hold the foundation of every sound ever synthesized.

w2_wave.name: The Waveform of Mastery
w2_wave.instruction: Name the wave. You have rolled this die before.

w2_cut.name: The Filter's Threshold
w2_cut.instruction: Where does the Sieve draw its line?

w2_rev.name: The Space of the Test
w2_rev.instruction: Place your sound in a space. Roll.

flanger.title: The Doppler Crossing

npcQuote.name: Delia Derbyshire
npcQuote.text: I ran the same tape past two machines at slightly different speeds. For a moment the two copies aligned. The sound it made — that metallic swoosh — was not in the recording. It was between them.

lore: Flanging was not invented. It was discovered by BBC engineers who slowed a tape reel with a thumb pressed against its flange. Two copies of the same signal, slightly out of phase, produce a comb filter: periodic notches across the frequency spectrum that sweep as the delay changes.

The Doppler Revenant drifts through Moogham's older districts in a halo of its own echo — a ghost that exists slightly behind and slightly ahead of itself simultaneously. It does not know it is delayed. It believes it is the original. The copy that drifted has forgotten being a copy.
{hunter}: the Revenant's vulnerability is its own periodicity. Find the rate at which it sweeps and match it.
victoryLore: The flange collapses. The Doppler Revenant stops drifting — for the first time in its existence, it occupies a single moment.
Flanger unlocked. The comb filter is yours: signal meets its own delayed self, and both subtract from the silence between them.
flanger.victoryTheory: Flanging: a signal mixed with a very short, slightly varying delay of itself (1–20ms). Where the two copies are in phase, they reinforce. Where out of phase, they cancel — creating notches in the spectrum. As delay time varies via LFO, notch frequencies sweep up and down, creating the characteristic jet-plane sweep. Key parameters: delay time (notch spacing), rate (sweep speed), depth (modulation amount), feedback (resonance at notch frequencies). Flanger = chorus with shorter delay and feedback.

fl_rate.name: The Ghost's Drift Speed
fl_rate.instruction: How fast does the Revenant slip out of phase? Roll.

fl_depth.name: The Echo's Separation
fl_depth.instruction: How far does the copy drift before returning? Roll.

bitcrush.title: The Decimated Quarter

npcQuote.name: Richard D. James
npcQuote.text: I deliberately destroy the signal. Not to ruin it — to find what it is after you've taken most of it away. What survives is the essential thing.

lore: Bit depth determines how many discrete values exist to represent a signal's amplitude. At 16 bits: 65,536 values. At 4 bits: 16. The fewer the values, the more audible the quantization noise — a coarse, digital grittiness generated by the rounding process itself.

The Decimated Horror is what remains when a sound has been reduced to its lowest representable state. It is not broken. It is simplified to the point of aggression. Every smooth contour replaced with stairs. Every vowel replaced with a bark.
{hunter}: reduce the signal. Understand that lo-fi is not a failure of quality — it is a deliberate mapping of a continuous world onto a finite grid.
victoryLore: The Horror's stepped waveform resolves. {hunter} has looked at a signal stripped to its essential structure and found it beautiful.
Bitcrusher unlocked. Quantization noise and sample rate reduction are now weapons, not accidents.
bitcrush.victoryTheory: Bit crushing reduces bit depth (amplitude resolution) and/or sample rate. Bit depth reduction adds quantization noise — smooth waveforms become staircases. Sample rate reduction creates aliasing — high frequencies fold back as inharmonic artifacts. Classic 8-bit and 12-bit sounds (Akai MPC60, E-mu SP-12) are beloved for their grit. Bitcrushing treats limitation as timbre.

bc_bits.name: The Depth of Reduction
bc_bits.instruction: How many bits remain? Roll — fewer is more brutal.

bc_rate.name: The Sample Rate Reduction
bc_rate.instruction: Roll — fewer samples per second means more aliasing.

spectral.title: The Frequency Loom

npcQuote.name: Curtis Roads
npcQuote.text: The spectrum is the score. Every sound is a chord you haven't named yet.

lore: Spectral processing operates in the frequency domain. Where a filter attenuates a band of frequencies, a spectral processor can rearrange, freeze, stretch, or invert individual frequency bins — each one a separate voice in the chord that any sound already is.

The Spectral Weave exists in both domains simultaneously. In the time domain it is a sound. In the frequency domain it is a constellation — hundreds of points of amplitude and phase, rotating slowly. It does not move through space. It moves through spectrum.
{hunter}: spectral processors reveal that every sound is already a composition. The vocoder, the phase vocoder, the FFT resynthesizer — all of them read the score already written inside the waveform.
victoryLore: The Spectral Weave's constellation collapses to a single point, then expands to silence.
{hunter} has understood that a waveform is already a chord. Spectral processing unlocked.
spectral.victoryTheory: Spectral processing analyzes sound via FFT, decomposing it into frequency bins. Operations include: freezing (hold bin amplitudes — the pad effect), smearing (blur over time), shifting (move bins up/down — inharmonic pitch shift), stretching (increase spacing — slow time without changing pitch). The vocoder cross-applies one sound's spectral envelope to another's pitch content. All spectral tools read the chord inside the waveform.

sp_vowel.name: The Spectral Vowel
sp_vowel.instruction: Which formant cluster does the Weave occupy? Roll.

sp_rate.name: The Weave's Drift
sp_rate.instruction: How quickly does the spectrum rotate? Roll.

resonator.title: The Cathedral Chambers

npcQuote.name: Pauline Oliveros
npcQuote.text: Deep listening is hearing what the space adds. Every room is a resonator. Every body is a resonator. The sound you make is completed by the frequencies it awakens.

lore: A resonator is a cavity that emphasises specific frequencies. The resonator does not produce sound — it selects it. When you sing into a resonant cavity, some frequencies are amplified and others absorbed. What emerges is not your voice — it is your voice filtered through the cavity's preferences.

The Resonant Choir occupies the Cathedral Chambers. It is not many voices. It is one void that has learned to emphasise specific frequencies with enough intensity that the result is perceived as many. Each chamber resonates at a different pitch. Together, they produce what sounds like a choir — but is actually the room, singing itself.
{hunter}: find the resonant frequency. Set the Q high enough that the filter sings back. When a filter resonates at its own cutoff, it has become an oscillator.
victoryLore: The Choir falls to one tone, then silence.
{hunter} has understood that a resonator is a filter with enough feedback to become a voice. Resonator unlocked — tuned resonance as synthesis technique.
resonator.victoryTheory: A resonator is a bandpass filter with very high Q. At extreme Q values, the filter self-oscillates — producing a pure sine at its cutoff frequency. Karplus-Strong synthesis uses a short delay loop with a lowpass filter to simulate a plucked string. Physical modeling generalises this: model the resonant properties of real instruments using digital filters tuned to their acoustic modes. The resonator knows only frequency and decay rate.

res_freq.name: The Chamber's Pitch
res_freq.instruction: Which frequency does the chamber prefer? Roll.

res_q.name: The Chamber's Sustain
res_q.instruction: How long does the resonance ring before it dies? Roll.

fm.title: The Bell Foundry Ruins

npcQuote.name: John Chowning
npcQuote.text: I was studying Doppler shifts in music, and I found that if you modulate the frequency fast enough, you don't hear the modulation as motion — you hear it as timbre. The sidebands are the sound.

lore: Frequency Modulation synthesis was discovered by John Chowning at Stanford in 1967. He increased the modulation rate past the threshold of auditory perception and found that instead of hearing motion, he heard harmonics. A sine wave modulated by another sine wave at audio rates produces sidebands: new frequencies at precise mathematical intervals above and below the carrier.

The Iron Bell Specter is one of the Foundry's last products — a bell cast with the wrong alloy, left to ring in the ruins. Its partials are inharmonic. The decay is wrong. But it is interesting, and interesting sounds survive in Moogham when correct ones do not.
{hunter}: set the ratio. Hear the sidebands. The Bell reveals itself when you find the numbers that describe it.
victoryLore: The Bell Specter's inharmonic ring resolves to a clean tone and fades.
FM synthesis unlocked — the ability to generate complex spectra from simple ingredients: two numbers, a carrier and a ratio, define the entire spectral content of an FM operator.
fm.victoryTheory: FM synthesis: a carrier oscillator's frequency is modulated by a modulator at audio rate. Sidebands appear at C ± M, C ± 2M, C ± 3M, etc. Integer C:M ratios produce harmonic spectra (musical). Non-integer ratios produce inharmonic spectra (bells, gongs). Modulation depth (index) controls sideband amplitude — more depth = richer spectrum. The Yamaha DX7's six operators, each a sine wave, can describe virtually any acoustic instrument in the right algorithm.

fm_carrier.name: The Carrier Note
fm_carrier.instruction: Name the carrier — the bell's fundamental. Roll.

fm_ratio.name: The Operator Ratio
fm_ratio.instruction: The modulator-to-carrier ratio defines the timbre. Roll.

arpeggio.title: The Cascading Falls

npcQuote.name: Brian Eno
npcQuote.text: The arpeggio is the synthesizer's heartbeat. It is what happens when you tell a machine which notes exist and let it decide the order. The machine has no preference. That is the point.

lore: An arpeggiator takes a chord — notes held simultaneously — and plays them in rapid sequence. The synthesizer arpeggiator reverses the harp's motion: it takes simultaneity and turns it back into sequence, then plays that sequence at a speed that blurs back into harmony.

The Cascading Phantom is what remains of a melodic phrase looped until it forgot its original order. It no longer knows which note comes first. It plays all of them, in all orders, convinced each arrangement is correct. It has been here since before the Hunt began.
{hunter}: set the interval. Set the tempo. The pattern emerges from the mathematics, not from your intention. This is the arpeggiator's gift.
victoryLore: The Phantom's sequence resolves to a single note, sustained.
Arpeggiator unlocked. Interval + tempo = pattern. The arpeggiator teaches that melody can be generated without composition.
arpeggio.victoryTheory: An arpeggiator steps through chord notes in sequence at a set tempo. Step interval determines harmonic quality. Speed determines whether the result sounds like melody (slow) or texture (fast). Classic arpeggios — Jarre's Oxygène, Tangerine Dream's Phaedra — defined electronic music by using limitation as structure.

arp_iv.name: The Step's Distance
arp_iv.instruction: What interval separates each note in the cascade? Roll.

arp_bpm.name: The Cascade's Speed
arp_bpm.instruction: How fast do the notes fall? Roll.

quantize.title: The Pitch Grid

npcQuote.name: Karlheinz Stockhausen
npcQuote.text: In serial music, pitch is controlled to the semitone. In electronic music, pitch is continuous. The quantizer is the treaty between those two worlds — it imposes the grid.

lore: Voltage-controlled synthesizers output any voltage — and voltage is continuous. The gap between C and C# contains infinite pitches. A quantizer watches the incoming CV and rounds it to the nearest legal pitch in a defined scale — snapping the continuous to the discrete.

The Pitch Warden has occupied the Grid since before the Healing Church marked it on their maps. It does not pursue. It simply corrects. Every sound that passes through its territory arrives at a legal scale degree, whether it intended to or not. The Warden does not destroy the out-of-tune note. It reassigns it.
{hunter}: name the scale. Name the root. Commit the law that will govern your voltages.
victoryLore: The Warden accepts {hunter}'s scale and steps aside.
Quantizer unlocked. Any CV signal — however random — will now arrive at legal pitches. The drunk walk becomes a melody.
quantize.victoryTheory: A quantizer samples incoming CV and rounds it to the nearest semitone or scale degree. Scale modes: chromatic, major, minor, pentatonic. With a quantizer downstream of a random source, you get generative melody — random voltages, musical notes. The quantizer is what distinguishes "random" from "random but in key."

q_root.name: The Law's Root
q_root.instruction: Which note anchors the scale? Roll.

q_step.name: The Scale Step
q_step.instruction: Which interval does the Warden enforce? Roll.

clock.title: The Clockwork Ossuary

npcQuote.name: Daphne Oram
npcQuote.text: The clock does not make time. It marks it. Without the clock, each module lives in its own time. With it, they share one.

lore: A modular synthesizer has no inherent sense of time. Each module runs at its own rate unless told otherwise. The master clock is a pulse generator — a voltage spike at regular intervals — that all time-sensitive modules synchronise to.

The Timekeeper's Marrow is the oldest machine in this district. Its pulse has never stopped. Every device in the Clockwork Ossuary runs at its division — some at 1/1, some at 1/4, some at 1/16. The Ossuary is a polyrhythm machine. Every bone in it is a subdivision.
{hunter}: set the master tempo. Then set its division. The clock gives permission — everything else only happens because of it.
victoryLore: The Timekeeper's pulse synchronises to {hunter}'s tempo and holds.
Clock unlocked. The master pulse now belongs to you — and with it, the synchronisation of everything else.
clock.victoryTheory: The master clock outputs a pulse at BPM rate. Clock divisions: 1/1 = one pulse per beat; 1/4 = sixteenth notes; 1/16 = thirty-second notes. Multiplications run slower. In a modular system, the clock is the conductor. Every module that responds to gates waits for the clock's permission before it acts.

ck_bpm.name: The Master Pulse
ck_bpm.instruction: The clock sets the law of time. Roll your tempo.

ck_div.name: The Clock Division
ck_div.instruction: At what division of the master pulse does your module respond? Roll.

chaos.title: The Attractor Fields

npcQuote.name: Edward Lorenz
npcQuote.text: Predictability: does the flap of a butterfly's wings in Brazil set off a tornado in Texas? In a deterministic system, yes — if you know the initial conditions precisely. The problem is that you never do.

lore: Chaos theory describes systems that are deterministic — governed by equations — but sensitive to initial conditions to the point of practical unpredictability. The Lorenz attractor traces a butterfly shape in state space forever, spiralling around two fixed points, never crossing its own path.

The Formless Swarm occupies the Attractor Fields at the edge of Moogham's outer district. It is not random. Each member follows an exact rule. But the rule involves sensitivity to every other member's position, and those uncertainties compound.
{hunter}: chaotic modulation is a tool, not a failure. The Swarm's aperiodic output, routed to pitch, produces melodies that evolve without repeating — as alive as biology.
victoryLore: The Swarm's trajectory stabilises around a single attractor.
Chaos unlocked. Non-linear, aperiodic modulation is now yours — patterns that evolve forever without repeating.
chaos.victoryTheory: Chaos synthesis uses the output of a chaotic differential equation (Lorenz, Rössler, Chua's circuit) as a control voltage. Unlike pseudo-random generators, chaotic signals are deterministic. But tiny changes in starting values produce wildly different trajectories. Applied to pitch: endlessly evolving melody. Applied to filter: breathing, living texture. Applied to amplitude: organic dynamics no LFO can fake.

ch_step.name: The Attractor's Velocity
ch_step.instruction: How far does the Swarm leap each event? Roll.

ch_rate.name: The Swarm's Density
ch_rate.instruction: How frequently does the chaos update? Roll.

samplehold.title: The Frozen Moment Archive

npcQuote.name: Max Mathews
npcQuote.text: The computer samples the world 44,000 times per second. But what you need is not the world. You need this one moment — held until you decide to release it.

lore: Sample and Hold captures an input voltage at a moment in time and holds it constant until the next clock pulse triggers a new sample. Connected to a noise source, it produces stepped random voltages — a staircase that takes a new random height at each clock tick.

The Moment Collector has been cataloguing Moogham's sounds since before the Hunt. It does not record the entire signal — only the value it finds at the moment of its trigger. Every past moment is stored in the Archive. None of them are accessible. The Collector only ever offers the present value, held until the next pulse replaces it.
{hunter}: sample the noise. Hold the value. Understand that musical structure can emerge from freezing randomness at regular intervals.
victoryLore: The Collector takes {hunter}'s sample and holds it steady.
Sample and Hold unlocked. Stepped random voltage — noise sampled at a clock rate — is now yours.
samplehold.victoryTheory: S&H samples an input voltage when triggered, holds it until the next gate. Typical use: noise → S&H → quantizer → VCO pitch = random melody in key. The step height is determined by input at trigger time; duration by clock rate. At slow rates: pitched random notes. At fast rates: tremolo-like rapid variation.

sh_seed.name: The Sampled Moment
sh_seed.instruction: Roll — this is the value the Collector captures.

sh_rate.name: The Trigger Rate
sh_rate.instruction: How frequently does the Collector take a new sample? Roll.

attenuvtr.title: The Inversion Chamber

npcQuote.name: Don Buchla
npcQuote.text: The attenuverter is the most powerful utility module in the system. It multiplies by any number between minus one and plus one. That's it. That's everything.

lore: An attenuverter attenuates and inverts. Full clockwise: signal passes unchanged. Center: muted — multiplied by zero. Full counter-clockwise: inverted and at full amplitude. The LFO that opened the filter now closes it. The envelope that increased volume now decreases it.

The Signal Inverter occupies a chamber beneath the Archive where Moogham's most fundamental utilities were maintained. It is not impressive. It has no oscillators, no filters, no modulation. It only multiplies. But multiplication by minus one is the difference between a parameter rising and falling.
{hunter}: the most powerful concepts in a modular system are the simplest. Multiply. Invert. Scale. These operations are the grammar that makes vocabulary useful.
victoryLore: The Signal Inverter sets {hunter}'s scaling factor and holds.
Attenuverter unlocked. Any modulation signal can now be scaled from 0 to full, or inverted — turning positive motion into negative.
attenuvtr.victoryTheory: An attenuverter multiplies input signal by a factor from -1 to +1. Positive: attenuate without inverting. Zero: mute. Negative: invert and attenuate. Key uses: inverting LFO to make filter close instead of open; scaling mod wheel to control modulation amount; adding DC offset to shift parameter center. Without attenuverters, modular synthesis is half-dimensional — only positive control, only opening, only rising.

av_amt.name: The Attenuation Factor
av_amt.instruction: How much signal passes through? Roll.

av_mod.name: The Modulation Depth
av_mod.instruction: How far does the attenuated signal drive the destination? Roll.

mixer.title: The Signal Confluence

npcQuote.name: Alan Parsons
npcQuote.text: The mix is not the last thing you do. It is the first decision you made, replayed. Every choice during recording becomes a constraint in the mix.

lore: A mixer sums multiple signals into one. In audio: multiple instruments into one stereo output. In CV: multiple modulation sources into one control destination. The mixer does not alter signals — it sums them. But if both signals are at full amplitude, the sum may clip. Gain staging is the art of mixing.

The Great Balancer stands at the Confluence where every cable in Moogham's second district eventually terminates. It is not a processor. It only adds. But the architecture of what flows into it determines what Moogham sounds like from the outside.
{hunter}: balance requires judgment about relative importance. The mix is not the last step — it is the evidence of every decision you made before it.
victoryLore: The Great Balancer accepts {hunter}'s levels and holds the sum steady.
Mixer unlocked. Multiple signal paths can be combined at any ratio — audio or CV, in any combination.
mixer.victoryTheory: A mixer sums multiple inputs, each with independent level control. Gain staging prevents summing from exceeding headroom. In CV mixing: summing two modulation sources creates additive modulation. Subtractive mixing (one positive, one inverted) cancels components. A VCA is a one-channel mixer whose level is controlled by CV — the same concept at different scales.

mx_gain.name: The Channel Gain
mx_gain.instruction: How loud does this signal arrive at the sum? Roll.

mx_blend.name: The Wet/Dry Balance
mx_blend.instruction: How much processed signal blends with the dry? Roll.

xy.title: The Parameter Plane

npcQuote.name: Isao Tomita
npcQuote.text: I do not play notes. I navigate a space. The hands know the map; the ears follow the path.

lore: An XY pad maps two parameters onto a two-dimensional plane. Moving horizontally changes one parameter; moving vertically changes another. The position of your touch defines a point in parameter space — two simultaneous values. Unlike a knob, which controls one dimension, the XY pad controls the relationship between two.

The Dimensional Cartographer has been charting Moogham's parameter spaces as long as the district existed. Every point on its surface is a combination of filter cutoff and LFO rate, or reverb mix and delay time. The map changes with the destination.
{hunter}: choose the axes. The Cartographer reveals what lives in the space between two parameters — places no knob can reach alone.
victoryLore: The Cartographer marks {hunter}'s position on the map and holds it.
XY Pad unlocked. Two-dimensional parameter control — drawing paths through timbral territory a single knob could never trace.
xy.victoryTheory: An XY controller outputs two simultaneous CV signals, one per axis. Common pairings: filter cutoff/resonance; reverb/delay; LFO rate/depth. The XY pad enables playing synthesis parameters with the same nuance as a melodic instrument. In software, it allows morphing between patches by moving through the space between preset positions.

xy_x.name: The X Axis — Filter
xy_x.instruction: Your horizontal position: filter cutoff. Roll.

xy_y.name: The Y Axis — Modulation
xy_y.instruction: Your vertical position: LFO rate. Roll.

theremin.title: The Contactless Cathedral

npcQuote.name: Clara Rockmore
npcQuote.text: The theremin demands that you listen with your hands. You cannot see the note. You must know where the pitch is in space — because your body is the instrument.

lore: Leon Theremin invented his instrument in 1919: two metal antennas, one for pitch, one for volume. The player's body capacitively couples to the antenna's electromagnetic field. No touch. No keys. No strings. The air between your hand and the antenna is the instrument.

The Untouched Voice floats in the Contactless Cathedral without settling. It has no contact with any surface. It moves by the electromagnetic attraction of the room's residual charge. The closer you get, the higher the frequency. Many hunters have backed away, uncertain. The ones who stayed learned something about the relationship between body and sound.
{hunter}: the theremin teaches that pitch is physical. Frequency is a spatial relationship. Your hand position IS the note.
victoryLore: The Untouched Voice settles on {hunter}'s chosen pitch and sustains.
Theremin unlocked. Gestural control of pitch — the body as the instrument, space as the keyboard.
theremin.victoryTheory: The theremin produces pitch by heterodyning two radio-frequency oscillators: one fixed, one variable (affected by hand proximity).
